author: NorthEast News Desk
body: Providence police arrested a 47-year-old man after a disturbance on Douglas Avenue in which a dog suffered a neck wound and required veterinary treatment.

Officers responded to 773 Douglas Avenue after receiving a report of a man armed with two knives, according to police information reported by NBC 10. Investigators said the man fled inside a residence while officers established contact. He later surrendered without a prolonged confrontation.

Police identified the suspect as Shah McKenney. The dog was taken to a veterinarian for treatment of a laceration to its neck; authorities had not released a detailed update on the animal’s condition at the time of the report.

McKenney faces two felony assault counts, malicious injury to an animal, disorderly conduct, obstruction and a charge involving prohibited weapons other than firearms. The charges reflect police allegations and have not been proven in court. The circumstances leading to the disturbance and the sequence in which the dog was injured remain part of the investigation.
dek: Police arrested a 47-year-old man after an armed disturbance on Douglas Avenue; an injured dog was taken for veterinary treatment.
headline: Providence man charged after dog injured during police disturbance
